stories.headline: Memes Highlight Gas Savings vs. 401(k) Losses After Democrat Midterm Wins
stories.hook: One week, folks saved $30 on gas. The next, their 401(k)s dropped $30,000 amid election fears.
stories.summary: After Democrats gained House and Senate majorities in the 2026 midterms, stock indexes fell sharply, hitting tech-heavy retirement accounts. Posters shared memes contrasting small gas price drops—like $30 to $35 per tank—with losses of $25,000 or more, often blaming a 'blue wave' and Democratic policies. Some lashed out at voters who prioritized cheaper fuel, while observers pointed to ongoing Republican control until January and other market factors like tech company news.

stories.headline: Hegseth Warns of Internal Threats and Cultural Suicide in Education
stories.hook: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth pointed to groups inside America hell-bent on tearing down core values, starting right in K-12 classrooms captured by progressive indoctrination.
stories.summary: In a widely shared video, Hegseth described America's greatest dangers as internal, driven by a loss of focus on foundational principles and an education system he called an indoctrination machine often fueled by foreign money. He stressed accountability as the key missing piece, with effects already showing in the Pentagon. Supporters called for action to protect the Republic, linking it to administration moves like state-led education reforms and school choice, while some posts question abolishing the federal Department of Education and cite shifting global demographics. Critics argue the views overlook other factors or lean partisan.

stories.headline: Democrats Remain Unpopular Despite Midterm Wins, Polls Show
stories.hook: Even after flipping seats in the 2026 midterms, Democrats face a tough reality: most voters worry they'll chase Trump probes over pocketbook issues.
stories.summary: CNN data analyst Harry Enten revealed the party's net favorability at -6 points post-election, far below peaks after 2006 and 2018 waves, calling it a rejection of Republicans rather than a Democratic mandate. A striking 67% of Americans, including nearly half of Democrats, fear the party will prioritize investigating the Trump administration over affordability and other key concerns. Leaders like Hakeem Jeffries (-17 points) and Chuck Schumer (-30 points) also trail in popularity, highlighting a disconnect between electoral gains and public sentiment as the new Congress begins.

stories.headline: Obama Advises House Democrats to Embrace Diversity and Avoid Complacency
stories.hook: In a closed-door meeting, Barack Obama looked at the new House Democratic freshmen and saw a true reflection of America — urging them to channel that diversity into real results.
stories.summary: Former President Obama met with the incoming class of House Democratic freshmen in Washington, arranged by Hakeem Jeffries, to discuss generational change, ideological differences, and delivering for constituents. He praised the caucus's diversity, contrasting it with a 'golf country club' on the other side of the aisle during State of the Union addresses, and warned against complacency while encouraging bolder pushes on health care beyond the Affordable Care Act. The remarks drew praise from supporters as a nod to broad representation but sharp criticism from conservatives, who called them divisive and pointed to Obama's own country club memberships.

stories.headline: Online Debate Erupts Over Embracing Elon Musk as Democrat
stories.hook: A simple question on X—'Would you embrace Elon Musk as a DEM?'—drew raw, heated responses from users across the political spectrum.
stories.summary: User Sinfulskin sparked the discussion on November 21, prompting replies ranging from harsh rejections like 'I wouldn’t embrace that fucking Nazi if he were dead' to support for Sen. Bernie Sanders' call to curb billionaire election spending. Sanders had criticized Musk and others for pouring $2 billion into races, labeling it oligarchy, especially after Musk admitted feeling 'pretty foolish' about his $500 million backing of Republicans in the 2026 midterms that Democrats won. Defenders highlighted Musk's job-creating companies and pointed to Democratic donors like George Soros, revealing deep divides on campaign finance and billionaire political roles.

stories.headline: U.S. College Faculty Shifted Sharply Left Over Decades
stories.hook: Back in 1969, professors leaned modestly left at 39-33. Today, that balance tips at least 6-to-1 across many schools, with elite disciplines hitting even steeper ratios.
stories.summary: Historical surveys like the 1969 Carnegie Commission showed conservatives sometimes outnumbering liberals in STEM fields, but recent data reveals a stark change: ratios now reach 108-to-0 Democrats in some anthropology departments and 56-to-0 in communications. Charts from Eric Kaufmann and Mitchell Langbert's 2018 analysis highlight heavy liberal concentrations in humanities and social sciences, while engineering and business remain more balanced. Commenters debate causes, from 20th-century institutional capture to cultural shifts, questioning if intellect differences or historical contingencies explain the trend.

stories.headline: Poll Shows 51% of Americans Back Deporting Most Illegal Immigrants
stories.hook: Even after the midterms, a new poll reveals steady public support for tougher immigration enforcement, with sharp divides across party lines.
stories.summary: A fresh Economist/YouGov survey of 1,628 U.S. adults from November 13-16 found 51% favor deporting all or most people who entered illegally, including 23% wanting everyone gone immediately and 28% allowing exceptions for those married to Americans or long-term residents without records. Support splits sharply: 83% of Republicans back it, while 41% overall prefer limiting deportations to serious criminals and independents nearly even at 47% for broad action. The results challenge claims of shifting voter views and highlight ongoing debates over enforcement amid political promises like amnesty.

stories.headline: Trump Reaffirms Deportation Stance Amid Poll Support
stories.hook: At a White House briefing, President Trump stood firm with charts showing public backing for deportations, pushing back against amnesty ideas from reporters.
stories.summary: Trump rejected broad legal status for 20 to 30 million illegal immigrants, declaring 'WE’RE NOT gonna let immigration destroy our country' while noting Hispanic support for deportations and border security. A new YouGov poll found 51 percent of Americans favor deporting most illegal immigrants, with only 7 percent wanting all to stay, though older surveys show support for limited paths for long-term residents. Officials like JD Vance criticized amnesty calls, and the administration appointed Stephen Miller as chief of staff, signaling focus on criminals and border enforcement despite some flexibility on DACA.
